- Identify a short list of **important business services** that, if disrupted, could threaten the firm’s safety and soundness, policyholder protection or the UK’s financial stability. [1][3]  
- Set an **impact tolerance** for each important business service, defining the maximum tolerable disruption length and other metrics. [7]  
- Conduct **scenario testing** (severe but plausible scenarios) to assess the firm’s ability to remain within impact tolerances and to learn from any failures. [5][6]  
- Produce a **self‑assessment** documenting compliance with the Operational Resilience Parts, including mapping of resources, testing strategy, lessons learned and improvement actions. [5]  
- Obtain **board approval** and regular review of the important business services, impact tolerances and self‑assessment, ensuring senior management has the necessary information and expertise. [4][7]  
- Establish clear **accountability** (e.g., a Chief Operations Senior Management Function) for implementing and reporting on operational resilience. [4]
